summary: A 100-foot Aermotor steel tower raised by the CCC on Valentine National Wildlife Refuge in the 1930s, still standing with its cab in place.

facts.design: Type MC-39 Aermotor steel tower, 100 ft high

access.note: On a national wildlife refuge; no source found on public access or climbing.

events.note: Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register as US 1847, NE 5

evidence.quote: Valentine Migratory Waterfowl Refuge was established in 1935 by an Executive Order of President Franklin Roosevelt.

evidence.supports: 70,000 acres bought as a breeding ground for wildlife
evidence.quote: Some 70,000 acres of land in the Sand Hills of Cherry County, Nebraska were purchased by the Bureau of Biological Survey “as a breeding ground for migratory birds and other wildlife.”

evidence.supports: worked with the Nebraska Game Preserve and Fish Commission
evidence.quote: The Nebraska Game Preserve and Fish Commission worked cooperatively with the Bureau of Biological Survey to bring the project to fruition.

evidence.supports: CCC crews on site by October 1935
evidence.quote: By October 1935, Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) workers had set up camp and started work under the direction of the Biological Survey.

evidence.supports: canal and diversion system to control lake water levels
evidence.quote: A system of canals and diversion works were planned to connect the lakes so that the Bureau could control the water level in each lake.

evidence.supports: WPA workers built 90 miles of fence near Hackberry Lake in August 1936
evidence.quote: In August 1936, 150 men from the Works Progress Administration (WPA) were also present in the refuge, building ninety miles of fence near Hackberry Lake.

evidence.supports: fence kept cattle out and marked the no-hunting area
evidence.quote: The fence would keep cattle out of the reserve and have the added benefit of delineating the area in which hunting was prohibited.

evidence.supports: tower is a 100-ft Aermotor MC-39 built by the CCC
evidence.quote: A Type MC-39 Aermotor steel tower, 100 feet high was erected by the CCC.

evidence.supports: Bureau of Biological Survey became US Fish & Wildlife Service in 1940
evidence.quote: (The bureau morphed into the US Fish & Wildlife Service in 1940).

evidence.supports: US Fish and Wildlife Service administers the tower
evidence.quote: Administered by U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service
Valentine NWR 2 – Pony Lake Cherry 42.47149 -100.48822 Tower Standing

evidence.supports: unmarked 'Standing' (vs 'Standing*') means the cab is still in place
evidence.quote: Towers that retain their structure and support with the cab no longer in place are denoted as “Standing * “

sources.title: Valentine NWR - Pony Lake Lookout Tower

notes_for_editor: The NHLR page narrates refuge-wide CCC/WPA history (canals, fencing) and separately states the tower itself was CCC-built, but gives no specific construction year for the tower. No source here covers staffing history, climbability, or visitor access, so those were left unknown rather than guessed.
